mutants.reason: Read FSM leaves ACK as soon as either the request is 0 or the write pointer is 0, so reads are released early and the flush check is bypassed; the read-side release timing and blocking during the software reset change.

This is the reset value of the ack retiming flop. It is only used when PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME=1, and the write FSM is in RUN right after reset, where the ack is ignored. The first clock edge reloads it with i_ack_rd before REQ or REL can read it, so no port can differ.
An accepted write no longer advances the write pointer, so o_full never asserts, stored words are overwritten and the read side never sees data.
When the pointers are equal the read-view occupancy becomes 2xDEPTH instead of 0, so o_empty and o_empty_thr are wrong.
With RETIME=0 the read side now sees the write pointer through an extra flop, so o_empty falls one cycle later than the exact model and gap-free streaming is lost.
The read pointer does not advance on an accepted read, so the same word is returned repeatedly and the occupancy never decreases.
The read-pointer clear condition is inverted, so the pointer is held at 0 in normal running and increments only in RST; reads return wrong data and the pointer is not reset by the software reset.
The write request flop is 1 in every state except HOLD, including RUN, so the read side is blocked permanently in normal operation and o_empty is stuck at 1.
The memory is written when i_wr_en is 0 and not when it is 1, so accepted words are not stored and read data is wrong.
When the next write pointer equals the read pointer the write-view occupancy becomes 2xDEPTH instead of 0, so o_full and o_full_thr are wrong when the FIFO is empty.
o_sw_rst_busy is inverted: it is 1 in normal running and 0 during the software reset sequence.

Reset value of the request retiming flop. With PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME=1 the read side sees a request right after reset, blocks o_empty and spuriously runs the read reset FSM for a few cycles, delaying the first word. It is invisible only when RETIME=0.

The write FSM leaves REL when the ack is low or the read pointer is 0, instead of both. o_sw_rst_busy can fall before the read side has been flushed, which changes the busy timing and writes can resume early.
o_sw_rst_busy resets to 1 instead of 0, so it is 1 during hardware reset and o_full is forced to 1.

The wrap compare uses 2xDEPTH instead of 2xDEPTH-1, so the pointer wraps only by truncation. This breaks the modulo-2xDEPTH range for depths that are not a power of two (such as 5 or 12), giving wrong flags and addresses. It happens to be harmless for depth 8.
The read FSM goes RUN to RST when no request is visible, so reads are blocked and the pointer is cleared in normal operation and o_empty stays 1.
The read block term is inverted: reads are blocked in RUN and allowed during the software reset, so o_empty is stuck at 1 in normal operation.

The read pointer wrap compare uses 2xDEPTH instead of 2xDEPTH-1, so the wrap relies on truncation. Non-power-of-2 depths (such as 5 or 12) then get a wrong pointer range, occupancy and read address. It happens to be harmless for depth 8.
The ACK exit condition checks the visible write pointer is non-zero instead of zero, so the read side stays blocked after the software reset or is released at the wrong time.
The write pointer wrap condition is inverted, so the pointer is cleared or incremented at the wrong values and wraps incorrectly, corrupting address, order and full.
The reset branch is inverted, so the write-domain flops are held at reset values while i_rst_n_wr is high and run normally during reset.
With RETIME=0 the write FSM sees the read ack through an extra flop, so the REQ to PTR and REL to RUN transitions and the o_sw_rst_busy duration shift by one cycle.
o_underflow resets to 1 instead of 0, so it shows a pulse during hardware reset.
o_full_thr resets to 1 instead of 0, so it is 1 during hardware reset and until the first write clock edge after release.

The inverted compare yields the wrong memory read address for depths that are not a power of two (such as 5 or 12), so the wrong word is shown. For depth 8 the address truncation to LPARA_ADDR_W bits hides the change.
With RETIME=0 the read side sees the request through an extra flop, so the read block starts one cycle after o_sw_rst_busy rises and a read can be accepted while busy is 1.
o_empty resets to 0 instead of 1, so it is 0 during hardware reset and until the first read clock edge after release.
The empty flop is loaded with the inverse of the empty condition, so o_empty is 1 when there is data and 0 when empty.
The REL exit requires the visible read pointer to be non-zero instead of zero, so the write FSM does not return to RUN after the flush and o_sw_rst_busy stays 1 or ends at the wrong time.
HOLD is left while i_rst_n_sw is low instead of high, so the sequence ends during a long low level and o_sw_rst_busy does not stay 1 while i_rst_n_sw is held low, and it holds when it is high.
With RETIME=0 the write side sees the read pointer through an extra flop, so o_full and o_full_thr fall one cycle later than the exact model and the flush check in REL is delayed.

The read ack resets to 1 instead of 0. If i_rst_n_rd is asserted alone while the write FSM waits in REQ or REL, the write FSM sees a false ack and advances or waits wrongly. It is invisible only when both resets are asserted together.
o_overflow resets to 1 instead of 0, so it shows a pulse during hardware reset.
The read-domain reset branch is inverted, so read flops are held at reset values while i_rst_n_rd is high and run normally during reset.
o_empty_thr resets to 0 instead of 1, so it is 0 during hardware reset and until the first read clock edge after release.
The read ack is inverted: it is 1 in RUN and 0 in ACK, so the write FSM leaves REQ immediately and does not see the acknowledge at the right time, breaking the software reset handshake.
